reading.body:
H.R. 6984 is a data center transparency bill with 15 cosponsors, all but two of them Democrats, and it has drawn lobbying from Google, a teachers union, and a California water district.

The cosponsor list is the clearest signal in the data. Fourteen Democrats and two Republicans, Brian Fitzpatrick and Michael Lawler, back a bill whose tagged issues are energy and data centers. That is a party-line-leaning coalition on an infrastructure question, not a bipartisan consensus.

The lobbying filings are the more interesting part for AI. Google is an obvious name here, but the American Federation of Teachers and the Santa Clara Valley Water District are not. A water district lobbying on a data center bill points at the part of AI scaling that runs through local utilities and land, not through model development. The data does not say what any of the three asked for, only that the bill was named as an issue in their filings.

What the data does not cover: the bill's actual provisions, its committee status, any recorded votes, or whether it has moved since the January 2026 status date. It also does not say whether the lobbying filings supported or opposed the bill. The cosponsor count and the filing count are the whole of what is here.

summary: H.R. 6984, Data Center Transparency Act. Latest status date 2026-01-08. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: energy and data centers. 4 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
